field_content.anomaly_check: Representations paired with their conjugates cancel perturbative gauge anomalies; no Standard Model assignment. A Z2 distinguishing original and conjugate fermions excludes direct cross-sector bare bilinears in the declared model.
field_content.fermions: chi,psi in(27,3) and chi_tilde,psi_tilde in(27*,3*) with conjugate Yukawa tensors and equal |y|
field_content.higher_operators: Dimension-five and gradient-completion coefficients set to zero for this renormalizable loop test; their loop corrections are not included.
field_content.potential: V_D=(1/2)sum g_a^2 mu_a^2; no polynomial T selector added
field_content.scalar: one complex Phi in(27,3) with canonical kinetic norm

full_one_loop.angular_reduction: 64 pi^2 V1_angular=(4g^4/9-8|y|^4) F(q), F=sum sigma^4 log(sigma^2); all subtraction/scale terms are radial by the exact mirror design law
full_one_loop.boundary: Full one-loop field determinant for this declared model on the D-flat plane. No full higher-order EFT, two-loop calculation, off-plane global minimization or measured vacuum is claimed.
full_one_loop.formula: 64 pi^2 V1 = 3 sum mV^4(log(mV^2/mu^2)-5/6)+sum mS^4(log(mS^2/mu^2)-3/2)-8 sum mF^4(log(mF^2/mu^2)-3/2)

interval_sign_proof.conclusion: T is a saddle for either overall bosonic or fermionic sign; this simplest shared mass-loop spectrum does not select the polynomial T minimum
interval_sign_proof.function: F=sum_m multiplicity*m^4*log(m^2) for the declared mirror mass law
interval_sign_proof.scope: Interval sign proof is for the declared mirror loop function. Its identification with the normalized 81-field mass pencil is checked numerically below, not symbolically certified.

full_one_loop.result: T is a saddle whenever the coefficient is nonzero; at its cancellation it is angularly flat at one loop, not an isolated minimum.
full_one_loop.scheme: MSbar Landau gauge on D-flat constant backgrounds; 3 massive-vector,1 real-scalar and8 paired-fermion degrees per matched cubic singular value

gauge_mass_identity.gauge_spectrum: 78 nonzero squared gauge masses equal g_E6^2/3 times the cubic squared singular masses; eight gauge zeros

gauge_mass_identity.method: rational Hermitian bases, exact inverse trace Grams; no rounding or floating eigenspectrum proof
gauge_mass_identity.normalization_boundary: This is a specified relative gauge normalization, not a prediction of measured gauge couplings.
gauge_mass_identity.scalar_spectrum: V_D=(1/2)sum_a g_a^2 mu_a^2 gives the same78 massive real scalar eigenvalues,78 Goldstone zeros and6 Cartan zeros

scale_dynamics.angular_boundary: For B>0 the T saddle remains; radial transmutation does not supply a joint stable T vacuum.
scale_dynamics.dilaton_model: r=x*s, Lambda_heat=alpha*s, Lambda_EFT=beta*s, V=s^4 U(x), M_Pl^2=s^2 K(x)
scale_dynamics.dilaton_stationarity: dV/dr=0 => Uprime(x)=0; dV/ds=0 then requires U(x)=0. A nonzero stationary s remains flat; a classical homogeneous potential cannot fix the absolute scale.
scale_dynamics.positive_single_heat_action: Leading volume and two-derivative EH terms: M_Pl^2=kappa Lambda_heat^2 Theta_F/(24 pi^2); V_volume=kappa Lambda_heat^4 Theta_F/(4 pi^2)
scale_dynamics.scale_boundary: Cutoff promotion supplies a named dynamical variable, not an absolute scale or tiny cosmological constant. An anomaly/transmutation scale or independent dimensionful datum remains required; loop corrections/counterterms can change the displayed single-heat-action relation.
scale_dynamics.stationary_radius: r0=mu exp[-A/(2B)-1/4], stable radially iff B>0
scale_dynamics.vacuum_value: -B r0^4/2 before an independent vacuum counterterm
